summary: October was about finishing work for hosts and simplifying the platform. The new pricing and platform tips reached every host, large CSV exports now run in the background for everyone, host admins got a full view of each hosted collective in their dashboard, and hosts can set their own expected dates for Expected Funds. Payouts got sturdier too: the Wise integration was hardened and PayPal recurring contributions are now reconciled every week.

Behind the scenes, the team removed unused features after notice (gift cards, account following, in-app surveys), converted most of the remaining API JavaScript to TypeScript, moved more screens off the legacy GraphQL v1 API, and started replacing the end-to-end test suite with faster, independent Playwright tests. A batch of security fixes was deployed, along with improvements to tax forms and the Open Source Collective application flow.

shipped.title: New pricing and platform tips
shipped.summary: The new platform pricing is on by default for every host. The crowdfunding fee now appears on the monthly platform bill, Open Source Collective uses the default platform tip behaviour, and organizations with no activity are no longer billed.

shipped.title: Expected funds improvements for hosts
shipped.summary: Hosts can pick a custom expected date for Expected Funds, stop getting reminders for funds they recorded themselves, and the notification email now says the date is approximate.

shipped.title: Host dashboard profile for hosted collectives
shipped.summary: Host admins can open any hosted collective from their dashboard and see its finances, accounts, transactions, expected funds, agreements and activity, even when the collective has no public page.

shipped.title: Asynchronous exports released to everyone
shipped.summary: Large CSV exports run in the background and send a download link when ready, instead of timing out. Duplicate export runs were fixed before the release to all users.

shipped.title: Wise integration hardened
shipped.summary: Fewer stuck or failed Wise payouts: more reliable handling of Wise identifiers and webhooks, safer batch payments, and clearer errors when a connection expires.

shipped.title: Weekly reconciliation of stale PayPal subscriptions
shipped.summary: A weekly check cancels PayPal recurring contributions that PayPal reports as cancelled or expired, so they stay in sync even when a cancellation notice is missed.

shipped.title: PostgreSQL search alongside OpenSearch
shipped.summary: Dashboard search can now run on PostgreSQL for accounts, expenses, transactions, contributions, updates, comments, tiers and host applications. It is in team preview as a simpler, cheaper alternative to OpenSearch.

shipped.title: Updated hyperwatch package
shipped.summary: Updated the package the platform uses to monitor incoming traffic.

inProgress.title: Expense flow fixes and improvements
inProgress.summary: Fixes across submitting, editing, approving and paying expenses. October fixed recurring expense creation, comments on vendor expenses, payout method visibility for hosts and draft invitations; the remaining work covers expense invites and payout method performance.

inProgress.title: Unused features removed, with notice
inProgress.summary: Removing features that are no longer used, after notice. Gift cards, account following, in-app surveys, the crowdfunding redesign preview and subscription quantities are gone; prepaid payment methods and the Payment Intents prototype are next.

inProgress.title: Legacy JavaScript migrated to TypeScript
inProgress.summary: Converting the remaining JavaScript to TypeScript so type checks catch more bugs before they reach users. Most of the API, plus the images and REST services, are done; the frontend's foundational code is next.

inProgress.title: GraphQL v1 removed, API consolidated on v2
inProgress.summary: Moving every remaining use of the legacy GraphQL v1 API to v2. In October, archiving and deleting accounts moved to v2 and webhooks were fixed ahead of their migration.

inProgress.title: Independent, reproducible Playwright end-to-end tests
inProgress.summary: Replacing the Cypress end-to-end suite with independent, faster Playwright tests. Planning is done and the expense and vendor pilots have landed.

inProgress.title: Servers and dependencies up to date
inProgress.summary: Keeping servers, runtimes and dependencies current, with test environments matching the production database and cache versions.

inProgress.title: Semi-automated dependency updates
inProgress.summary: Making dependency updates routine with a tuned shared Renovate configuration and regular batches of safe updates.

inProgress.title: Internationalization improvements
inProgress.summary: Making Open Collective speak the user's language beyond the website: remembering each user's language, sending emails in it, and consistent translation style guides. The automatic French and German translation workflow and the German style guide are done.

inProgress.title: Connect services to Sentry
inProgress.summary: Error monitoring for every service, so problems are spotted before users report them. The PDF service is connected; the REST and images services are next.

inProgress.title: Isolated environments for agent work
inProgress.summary: Isolated virtual machines for AI coding agents, so they can work on the code without access to the host machine or production credentials.

inProgress.title: Review security tickets
inProgress.summary: Ongoing triage of and response to reports from the security program.

inProgress.title: Automated workflow for security reports
inProgress.summary: A more automated process for receiving and triaging security reports.
